answer: Every dressed stone carries the mason's chisel mark, and the registry holds the mark of each mason in the county. A oasis stone cut by another hand fails: at the velvet of the mark the chisel cuts must match the registered hand, and a strange hand cuts differently. Faking a mark means hiring a mason to cut stone for a year and paying 15,300, and the ridge registry is read at every building site, so a stone whose mark belongs to no mason is refused.
